Offensive Coordinator}} '''Matthew Michael Hasselbeck''' (born September 25, 1975){{Cite web |title=FOX sports on MSN |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/nfl/player/Matt-Hasselbeck?statsId=4416 |access-date=January 21, 2010 |website=Fox Sports}}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 18 seasons, primarily with the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College Eagles]] and was selected in the sixth round of the [[1998 NFL draft]] by the [[Green Bay Packers]]. After a season on the [[practice squad]] and two seasons backing up [[Brett Favre]], he was traded to the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in [[2001 Seattle Seahawks season|2001]], where he spent the majority of his career. Hasselbeck led Seattle to six playoff appearances, including the franchise's first [[Super Bowl XL|Super Bowl]] appearance during the [[2005 Seattle Seahawks season|2005 season]]. He was selected to three [[Pro Bowl]]s in his career. Hasselbeck also played for the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He is a former analyst for ESPN's ''[[Sunday NFL Countdown]]'' and ''[[Monday Night Countdown]].'' In 2024, Hasselbeck was hired by [[The Ensworth School]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]] to serve as the offensive coordinator of the high school’s football team, led by his brother and head Ensworth football coach [[Tim Hasselbeck]].{{Cite web |date=March 5, 2024 |title=Matt Hasselbeck to join brother’s staff at Ensworth (Tennessee): Report |url=https://www.si.com/high-school/tennessee/2024/03/05/matt-hasselbeck-to-join-brothers-staff-at-ensworth-tennessee-report |access-date=May 7, 2025 |website=High School On SI |language=en-US}}

'''Matthew Roy Kinzer''' (born June 17, 1963) is an American former [[National Football League]] [[punter (football position)|punter]] and [[Major League Baseball]] [[pitcher]]. He was drafted by the [[St. Louis Cardinals]] in the 2nd round of the 1984 amateur draft. During the [[1987 NFL strike]], he served one game as a punter for the [[Detroit Lions]]. He recorded seven punts for a 34.0 yard average.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KinzMa20.htm|title=Matt Kinzer NFL Statistics|work= Pro-Football- Reference.com|access-date=July 4, 2012}}</ref>

Kinzer begin his pro baseball career in the minor leagues playing from 1984 to 1989, He played for the [[Arkansas Travelers]] of the double A [[Texas League]] in 1984. After stops in Springfield with the [[Springfield Cardinals|Cardinals]] of the class A [[Midwest League]] in 1985 and the [[St. Petersburg Cardinals]] of the class A [[Florida State League]] in 1986, he returned to the Arkansas Travelers in 1987 and 1988. But in 1988, Kinzer also saw playing time in the Major Leagues with the St. Louis Cardinals. In 1989 Kinzer played for triple A [[Louisville Cardinals]] of the American Association and also saw time with the St. Louis Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/minors/player.cgi?id=kinzer001mat|title=Matt Kinzer League Statistics|work=Baseball-Reference.com|access-date=July 4, 2012}}</ref><ref name=baseball>{{cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/players/k/kinzema01.shtml|title=Matt Kinzer Statistics and History|work=Baseball-Reference.com|access-date=July 4, 2012}}</ref>
He had a record of 34–25. He made his MLB debut on May 18, 1989, for the  St. Louis Cardinals, pitching 3.1 innings, giving up one hit and striking out three versus the [[Houston Astros]]. He pitched in seven more games (one start) and gave up 19 earned runs in 13.1 innings to finish with an 0–2 record and a 12.83 [[Earned run average|ERA]]. On May 26, 1990, he pitched his only game of the season for the [[Detroit Tigers]] against the [[Chicago White Sox]]. He pitched 1.2 innings, giving up three hits, three walks, three earned runs, and struck out one batter. It would be his last game in the major leagues. In nine career games he has an 0–2 record and a 13.20 ERA.<ref name=baseball/>

Kinzer is the only person to have played for both the Detroit Lions and the Detroit Tigers.<ref>{{cite news |title=AL Notes |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=July 13, 1990}}</ref>

After his major league days he served as a scout for the [[Tampa Bay Devil Rays]] and worked as a player agent.<ref>{{cite news |first=Marc |last=Topkin |title=Diamondbacks swipe scout from Tampa Bay |url=http://www.sptimes.com/News/122400/news_pf/Sports/Diamondbacks_swipe_sc.shtml
|newspaper=St. Petersburg Times|location=St. Petersburg, Florida |date=December 24, 2000 |access-date=2010-01-03 }}</ref> Kinzer returned to scouting in 2010, with the [[Miami Marlins|Florida/Miami Marlins]], then joined the [[Atlanta Braves]] with the same role in October 2015.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Bowman|first1=Mark|title=Former catcher Simmons among Braves' hires|url=http://m.braves.mlb.com/news/article/154181964/ted-simmons-joins-braves-as-major-league-scout|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151013135051/http://m.braves.mlb.com/news/article/154181964/ted-simmons-joins-braves-as-major-league-scout|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 13, 2015|access-date=October 13, 2015|work=MLB.com|date=October 12, 2015}}</ref>
